name: scrotal pain and masses overview
title: Scrotal pain and masses decision chart: acute pain sorted by onset into testicular torsion (surgery within 6 to 8 hours) or epididymo-orchitis (antibiotics), with trauma pointing to a hematocele; a scrotal mass sorted on exam and ultrasound into hydrocele or inguinal hernia, varicocele, spermatocele or testicular cancer, each with what confirms it and what to do

root.title: Scrotal pain or a lump: SUDDEN pain, or a MASS?
lines: ask: onset (sudden or gradual) · worse with movement · urinary symptoms · trauma · previous episodes
the HISTORY separates torsion (surgery) from infection (antibiotics)

groups.title: ACUTE PAIN: how did it START?
lines: after TRAUMA → hematocele (blood in the tunica vaginalis): ultrasound to rule out testicular RUPTURE

groups.title: SUB-ACUTE pain or a MASS: exam + SCROTAL ULTRASOUND
lines: EVERY scrotal mass → urology: think of cancer first

head: h
Testicular torsion
SURGICAL EMERGENCY
pres: • testis ROCK HARD (blood in, none out)

head: h
Hydrocele or inguinal hernia
pres: • BABY: hydrocele open to the peritoneum
• ADULT: fluid in a closed sac
inv: PINCH the top of the scrotum

head: h
Testicular cancer
age 13–35
pres: • acute pain in a few · gynecomastia
• RISK: undescended or atrophic testis, prior cancer
inv: then surveillance, chemo or radiation by type and stage
